Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth registration completeness is very low; an analysis citing the 2015–16 Angola DHS reports only 25% of children under five (and 12% under one year) were registered, implying <20% completeness for the youngest cohort and low overall CRVS uptake.
revision_notes: Fetched the cited ScienceDirect article: it reports the 2015-16 Angola DHS found 25% of children under five registered (12% under one year). This 25% under-five figure was already mis-banded in the original row — it falls in the 20-49% range (code 2), not <20% (code 1), so the original score did not match its own cited evidence. Searched for and fetched the newer Angola IIMS/DHS 2023-24 survey reports (INE, MINSA and ICF, published January-May 2025), which show birth registration for children under five rising to 38% (up from 25% in 2015-16), corroborated by Angolan press reporting on the survey. 38% falls within the 20-49% band, code 2. Score revised from 1 to 2 on the strength of the newer primary survey data.
revised_comments: Civil registration coverage remains moderate: the Angola IIMS/DHS 2023-24, conducted by the Instituto Nacional de Estatística with the Ministry of Health and ICF, finds that 38% of children under five have a registered birth, up from 25% in the 2015-16 survey. Coverage is markedly higher in urban than rural areas. This places overall civil register uptake in the 20-49% band.
